facts: For a velocity–time graph in m/s against seconds, $\int_a^b v(t)\,dt$ gives displacement in metres. It also gives distance travelled when $v(t)\geq0$ throughout the interval.
Write the model as a definite integral before calculating: total change $=\int_{a}^{b}R(t)\,dt$.
A region bounded by a curve and an axis, both measured in metres, has an area in $\text{m}^{2}$.
Where the rate is negative the quantity is falling, so that part of the integral is subtracted.
Displacement is the area above the velocity–time axis minus the area below it. Distance travelled is the integral of speed: split at any sign changes and add the absolute areas.
An area lying below the $x$-axis gives a negative integral, so take its absolute value for a physical size.
For equally spaced measurements, the trapezoidal rule gives an estimate: $\frac{h}{2}\left(f_0+f_n+2(f_1+\cdots+f_{n-1})\right)$, where $h$ is the spacing.
To find the amount remaining after a given time, add the net change to the initial amount.
steps: Write the quantity as a definite integral, or use the trapezoidal rule for supplied measurements
Evaluate the integral or calculate the estimate
Interpret the answer with its practical unit, adding the initial amount when required

foundation.question_text:
An object moves in the positive direction along the $x$-axis. Its velocity is measured at the following times.

| $t$ (seconds) | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v$ (m/s) | $2$ | $3$ | $5$ | $6$ | $8$ |

Use the trapezoidal rule to estimate the distance travelled in the first $4$ seconds.
foundation.solution_text:
The velocity is nonnegative, so the area under the velocity–time graph gives distance.
$h=1$
Distance $\approx\frac{1}{2}\left(2+8+2(3+5+6)\right)$
$=\frac{1}{2}(38)$
$=19\text{ m}$

foundation.question_text:
A trolley moves in the positive direction along a straight track. Its velocity is measured at the following times.

| $t$ (seconds) | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v$ (m/s) | $1$ | $4$ | $5$ | $2$ |

Use the trapezoidal rule to estimate how far it travels in the first $6$ seconds.
foundation.solution_text:
The velocity is nonnegative, so the area under the velocity–time graph gives distance.
$h=2$
Distance $\approx\frac{2}{2}\left(1+2+2(4+5)\right)$
$=21\text{ m}$

The volume added is the area under the rate–time graph.
Volume added $=\int_{0}^{5}(20+6t)\,dt$
$=\left[20t+3t^{2}\right]_{0}^{5}$
$=100+75$
$=175\text{ L}$
Final volume $=100+175=275\text{ L}$

The fuel used is the area under the rate–time graph.
Volume used $=\int_{0}^{3}\left(3t^{2}+4\right)dt$
$=\left[t^{3}+4t\right]_{0}^{3}$
$=27+12$
$=39\text{ L}$
Volume remaining $=80-39=41\text{ L}$

foundation.question_text:
A dam initially contains $1200$ litres of water. Water flows into it at a rate of $R=30+8t$ litres per hour, for $0\leq t\leq5$ hours.
How much water will be in the dam after $5$ hours?
foundation.solution_text:
Volume added $=\int_0^5(30+8t)\,dt$
$=\left[30t+4t^2\right]_0^5$
$=150+100$
$=250\text{ L}$
Final volume $=1200+250=1450\text{ L}$

The channel floor lies below ground level, so the integral is negative and the area is its absolute value.
$\int_{-4}^{4}\left(\frac{x^{2}}{4}-4\right)dx$
$=\left[\frac{x^{3}}{12}-4x\right]_{-4}^{4}$
$=\left(\frac{16}{3}-16\right)-\left(-\frac{16}{3}+16\right)$
$=-\frac{32}{3}-\frac{32}{3}$
$=-\frac{64}{3}$
The cross-sectional area is $\frac{64}{3}\text{ m}^{2}$.

development.question_text:
An object moves in the positive direction along the $x$-axis. Its velocity is measured at the following times.

| $t$ (seconds) | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v$ (m/s) | $2.1$ | $1.8$ | $2.2$ | $2.7$ | $3.1$ | $3.4$ |

Use the trapezoidal rule to estimate the distance travelled in the first $5$ seconds.
development.solution_text:
The velocity is nonnegative, so the area under the velocity–time graph gives distance.
$h=1$
Distance $\approx\frac{1}{2}\left(2.1+3.4+2(1.8+2.2+2.7+3.1)\right)$
$=\frac{1}{2}(25.1)$
$=12.55\text{ m}$

The rate is negative for $t>3$, so water leaves the tank after $3$ seconds and that area is subtracted.
Net change $=\int_{0}^{5}(6-2t)\,dt$
$=\left[6t-t^{2}\right]_{0}^{5}$
$=30-25$
$=5\text{ L}$
Final volume $=50+5=55\text{ L}$

development.question_text:
A lake's widths are measured at $12$-metre intervals along a straight baseline.

| Distance along baseline (m) | $0$ | $12$ | $24$ | $36$ | $48$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Width (m) | $0$ | $16$ | $21$ | $14$ | $0$ |

Use the trapezoidal rule to estimate the surface area of the lake.

A tank initially contains $800$ litres of water. Water flows into it at a rate of $R=4t+12$ litres per minute, for $0\leq t\leq10$ minutes.
Find the volume of water in the tank after $10$ minutes.

A tank initially contains $250$ litres of water. Water flows into it at a rate of $R=6t-t^2$ litres per minute, for $0\leq t\leq6$ minutes.
Find the volume of water in the tank after $6$ minutes.
development.solution_text:
Volume added $=\int_0^6(6t-t^2)\,dt$
$=\left[3t^2-\frac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^6$
$=108-72$
$=36\text{ L}$
Final volume $=250+36=286\text{ L}$

mastery.question_text:
A reservoir initially contains $90$ megalitres of water. Its net inflow rate is $R=15-4t$ megalitres per day, for $0\leq t\leq6$ days. A negative rate means water is being released.
Find the volume in the reservoir after $6$ days.
mastery.solution_text:
The signed integral gives the net change.
$\int_0^6(15-4t)\,dt$
$=\left[15t-2t^2\right]_0^6$
$=90-72$
$=18\text{ ML}$
Final volume $=90+18=108\text{ ML}$

mastery.question_text:
A drum initially contains $500$ litres of liquid. It loses liquid at a rate of $R=60e^{-0.25t}$ litres per minute, for $0\leq t\leq8$ minutes.
Find the volume remaining after $8$ minutes, correct to one decimal place.

A tank initially contains $1000$ litres of water. Water flows into it at a rate of $R=\frac{120}{t+2}$ litres per hour, for $0\leq t\leq6$ hours.
Find the volume in the tank after $6$ hours, correct to one decimal place.
